title: In Praise of the Flute
summary: Four verses in praise of the flute. It stands among instruments as the Gītā among scriptures and the Gaṅgā among rivers; the transverse flute (Kṛṣṇā) is as dear to music lovers as the Gītā; its practice yields the four aims of life; and it is sweet, cheap, light and open to rich and poor alike.

blocks.verse:
वाद्येषु बंशी निगमेषु गीता नदीषु गंगा नगरेषु काशी।
योगेषु भक्तिश्च जनेषु माता हितप्रियाभ्याम् सततं विशिष्टाः।।२।।
blocks.text: Among instruments the flute, among scriptures the Gītā, among rivers the Gaṅgā, among cities Kāśī, among yogas devotion, and among people the mother: these always stand out for being both beneficial and dear.

In the world there are only a few things or persons that are dear as well as beneficial. For example: among instruments the flute, which purifies the prāṇa (breath) and sounds sweet to the ears; among scriptures the Gītā, which purifies the mind through yoga and is dear for its simplicity; among rivers the Gaṅgā, which delivers [us] from many diseases and gives creatures sweet and cool water; among cities Kāśī, which frees [us] from many kinds of sin and charms the mind with its beauty; among yogas bhakti (devotion), supremely dear, which removes the darkness of ignorance and lights the lamp of knowledge; and among people the mother, who wishes [our] good and speaks kindly. All these hold a special place in the world.

blocks.verse:
योगेश्वरस्य कृष्णस्य यथा गीता जनप्रिया।
संगीते श्रद्दधानानाम् कृष्णावंशी तथा प्रिया।।३।।
blocks.text: Just as the Gītā of Kṛṣṇa, lord of yoga, is dear to people, so the Kṛṣṇā flute is dear to those who have faith in music.

Just as the Gītā of Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa is dear to people, in the same way the āḍī bansī (transverse, side-blown flute) is very dear to lovers of music. If he recited the Gītā to free Arjuna from delusion, he played the flute to free the gopīs from attachment.

blocks.verse:
ममापि कृष्णे भक्तिः स्यादिति वंशीम् भजाम्यहम्।
साधना चास्य वाद्यस्य धर्मार्थादि फलप्रदा।।४।।
blocks.text: Thinking 'may I too have devotion to Kṛṣṇa', I worship the flute; and practice of this instrument bestows the fruits beginning with dharma and artha (the four aims of life).
Thinking 'may I too have bhakti (devotion) for Śrī Kṛṣṇa', I worship the flute, because through its sādhanā (practice) the four fruits, dharma, artha, kāma and mokṣa, are obtained.

blocks.verse:
वाद्येषु रुचिरं मन्ये बंशीवाद्यं सुसप्तकम्।
माधुर्यादल्प मूल्यत्वा ल्लघुत्वात् सर्वसंभवात्।।५।।
blocks.text: Among instruments I consider the flute, with its fine seven notes, the most pleasing: because of its sweetness, because it costs little, because it is light, and because it can be had everywhere.
Since this instrument is within easy reach of the poor and the rich alike, and can be found anywhere from the forest to the market, who would not love this simple and sweet instrument?
